Considering the above, we are of the view that the Petitioner has taken adequate and timely steps to mitigate the prolonged outage, clearly visible from repeated followups, safety measures (anti-theft charging), escalation to NRPC/NRLDC, and implementation of the agreed bypass arrangement once feasible. The delay in restoration was beyond Petitioner’s control. 25. The question before the Commission is therefore limited to whether the Petitioner has fulfilled the statutory conditions under Clause 5(iii)(c) for the grant of deemed availability for the residual period of outage, i.e., from 1.5.2024 to 30.7.2024. In view of the findings in Issue No. 1 and Issue No. 2, the Commission is satisfied that (a) the outage is not attributable to the Petitioner; (b) the proximate cause lies entirely in the HVPNL’s substation equipment; (c) the Petitioner has taken all reasonable steps to mitigate the outage; and (d) the extended duration was occasioned by factors wholly beyond the control of the Petitioner, including OEM-dependent procurement timelines and the HVPNL’s restoration constraints. 28. Consequently, the Petitioner shall be entitled to recover the applicable transmission charges for the said period from the beneficiaries in accordance with Regulation 67 and the methodology prescribed in Appendix-IV of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. The Petitioner is directed to follow the established procedures and the relevant sharing regulations for computation and sharing of such transmission charges. 29. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of expenditure incurred by the Petitioner towards petition filing fee and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of the instant petition, in terms of Regulation 94(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 31. Further, the Commission in an order dated 11.1.2009 in Petition No. 109/2009 has already held that the filing fee will be reimbursed only in case of tariff petitions and will not be reimbursable in case of Miscellaneous Petitions. The relevant portion of the order dated 11.1.2009 is as follows: _Filing fees paid for filing the Review Petitions, Interlocutory Applications and other Miscellaneous Applications will not be reimbursed in tariff. The Commission has decided to reimburse the expenses on publication of notices as such expenses are incurred to meet the statutory requirement of transparency in the process of determination of tariff.”_ ## 32. The Commission’s regulations also do not provide for reimbursement of the filing fee in case of Miscellaneous Petitions. Therefore, the Petitioner’s prayer for reimbursement of the filing fee and other related expenditures in filing the instant petition is not allowed.
